© 2018 Radomír Věncek (Rada)

Welcome to Aviator! The Aviator is Android application – navigational tool for all aviators. Its main purpose is to help aviators to enjoy the flight and fly safely. It’s a perfect tool for powered paragliders as well as for powered hang gliders… but it could be used more or less by any aviator :-)

This application has been created to fulfill my personal requirements which I have not found implemented in other applications. I\'m avare of quite a few of them in the Google Play store however no one was \'good enough\' for me :-)

Some key features:
- Zero-touch app. control (you have all the necessary info on one screen during flight)
- Forced on screen (the app will return to foreground after configured time after accidental tap / button press)
- Google map integration - 2 themes (light / dark)
- Flight vector (1, 2 and 3 minutes vector)
- Air space visualization (supports AIXM, OFMX, Open AIP and Openair data formats)
- Flight plan support
- Route recording and export to KML (readable by Google Earth)
- Flight export to server xcontest.org (IGC format)
- Real time tracking (share your location with your group and be visible to other group members)
- …

Limitations

Please note that the Aviator mobile application is provided AS IS without warranty of any kind. This application doesn’t fulfill any formal requirements and/or regulations and can’t be formally used as a replacement of officially required flight equipment! Author of the application and its web site does NOT accept any responsibility or liability related to using the application.

Some key aspects you have to realize before and during every flight (or any other application usage):

(!) The application is using device\'s non-certified and potentially non-precision GPS and similarly potentially non-precission pressure sensors for all the positioning and movement data (location, altitude, speed, bearing, climb/descend rate) with all the possible consequences of this fact (e.g. entering controlled / restricted area without permission).

(!) Please realize what type of altitude you are using and displaying on screen. Be careful when using GPS altitude! This is more or less OK below the transition level, it\'s however definitely not OK above the transition altitude (where airplanes use flight levels on standard QNH 1013 hPa / 29.92 inHg instead of AMSL altitude) - especially when flying close to bottom border of a controlled airspace and in low pressure weather (below the standard pressure). When using pressure altitude don\'t forget to set correct local (area) or standard QNH in the settings!

(!) The installed air space file might not correspond to the real air space configuration. There is no automatic and reliable update functionality implemented. Always verify your flight plan against the official materials of your national aviation authorities, check actual status of all relevant temporary restricted / segregated areas, check NOTAMs, local procedures etc. This application does NOT contain such information!

(!) The Vertical profile shows only approximate / interpolated ground elevation. It calculates actual value from a matrix of cca 230x230 metres ground level matrix. And it could be very imprecise in hilly areas. Use this information only as a helper information. That\'s why it doesn\'t show any numbers. It\'s just for a high level awareness.

All of this however of course doesn\'t protect you to use the application to make your flight experience better :-)

Need help?

To understand all the application features in detail please check the application web site: aviator.freesite.host

Feedback?

I\'d love to hear from you - Aviators - your additional wishes - what would you see useful having in the application…? How can I make it better. Please contact me via this Facebook application page. You can find there also information about new features and versions and some useful tips and tricks for the application!

Thanks for downloading the app. Please note that you are now running a free version of the application with limited functionality. You can use it as long as you want however we recommend to spend a few bucks a year for a full and unlimited version.

There is a small difference between the free and full version of the application. The free version:
- allows only a single point in the flight plan (full version is unlimited here)
- allows only OpenAir air space file format (full version allows also AIXM, OFMX and Open AIP formats)
- doesn\'t allow to de/activate temporary spaces - all are always active (full version allows individual space de/activation)
- doesn\'t allow to export the flights to the xcontest.org server (full version does)
- doesn\'t allow to share your location with other pilots (full version does allow it)

In order to support further development of this application please purchase the full version. Thank you!

Air space
Here you can load your area air space definition file. This application has no access to guarantied and always up to date air space definition files.
However thanks to the projects Open Flightmaps (OFM - https://www.openflightmaps.org/) and the openAIP (https://www.openaip.net/) the application can use the great database of aeronautical data for many (mainly European at this moment) regions. The first option Download OFM data file shows list of available regions which you can download directly into the application. This application doesn\'t update the data automatically. Make sure that you check the data regularly to use always up to date data. This functionality is only available in the Full version of the application. Please purchase the subscription to enable the feature.
 
The 2nd option to load the airspace configuration into the application is to download the air space definition file and let the application read/parse it.
This application supports 3 different data formats:
- AIXM version 4.5 - this is the most comprehensive data format, it contains air space definitions as well as rich airport information
- OFMX - this is just an enriched version of the AIXM from OFM
- Open AIP - supports both air space definition file as well as airport info - in separate files
- Openair - just the air space definition file (no airport information)
The AIXM, OFMX and Open AIP data formats are only available in the Full version. Only the Openair format is available in the free version of the application.
 
You can download some airspace definition files for some areas here:
- https://www.openflightmaps.org/ - OFMX and Openair
- https://www.openaip.net/ - Open AIP
- http://soaringweb.org/Airspace/ - Openair
 
All the formats can contain air spaces of all known types including temporary areas like TRA and TSA. The Air space setup allows you to activate or deactivate particular temporary spaces if they are defined as temporary (in the Full version only).
 
The last option lets you to remove the air space definition file.
 
Note: Older devices with low memory have problems loading and parsing the very big air space files and may crash with Out of memory error. Then you need a newer device with more memory.

Air space
This screen contains list of all temporary areas split to 2 sections: TRA and TSA. After loading of the air space definition file all the areas are shown as active by default. Here you can mannually activate or deactivate individual areas or the whole area type.
 
You can expand/collapse the whole section by tapping on the area type line, you can activate (A as All) or deactivate all (N as None) areas of the particular type. Then you can de/activate individual area via its checkbox. Deactivated areas are shown differently on the map and its description is in italic font style (in the on map info view).   De/activation of temporary areas is only available in the Full version of the application. Please purchase the subscription to enable the individual temporary area de/activation.

Flight plan
Current position
Check your current position, your GPS coordinates and share them with anybody if you need to via the share button, e.g. as an SMS.
 
Flight plan
Here you can find your flight plan as a list of turn points (TP). You can add new TP via the + button in the action bar. For each TP you see its:
- name
- GPS coordinates
- distance (D) and bearing (B) from the previous TP
and a set of buttons to:
- select the TP as the next one
- up/down arrows to reorder the TP
- remove the TP from the flight plan
 
Small arrow left of one of the TP indicates current active TP you are flying to. Use the green point button to select a different TP if you need to.
 
The turn points can be added either on this screen or directly in the map via a long tap on any location or on an info window(!) of a registered point marker (VFR point, airport, POI).
 
You can only add one TP in the free version. You need to purchase the Full version in order to be able to add unlimited number of TPs.
 
Load flight plan
In the Full version you can also load a whole flight plan created in a 3rd party aviation planning tool. There are supported simple text formats (one turn point per line with just latitude longitude) and some XML formats whether GPX, KML or even Sky Daemon. Support of these formats is very limited and it\'s likely it won\'t read all possible variants of these files. If you find such not readable example of the flight plan file, send it to me, I\'ll update the Aviator to read it properly.
Loading a new Flight plan deletes any previous plan without further asking.

Flights
You will find here all your recorded flights. If you are not flying you can perform few actions on every flight. The action icon is disabled during flight. Actions:
- Details - shows a simple screen with some flight details
- View - loads the flight and shows it in the application, the view will be moved to the flight start position
- View in Google Earth - exports the flight to KML format, opens the Google Earth application (if installed) and shows the flight
- Export as KML - exports the flight to KML format and opens standard Android Share screen
- Export to xcontest.org - exports the flight into the IGC format and uploads it to the xcontest.org server (if configured) - Full version only!
- Delete - deletes the flight (permanently!)
 
Integration with the xcontest.org server is only available in Full version of the application. Go to the main menu, select Full version and purchase a yearly subscription to use this and few other extra features.
 
If you are missing your flights you have recorded using previous version of the application you can import them via the Import old flights option in the Settings screen.
 
If you uninstall the application from the phone, you lose all flights. So export all of them to KML and store or better, buy the Full version and upload them to the xcontest.org server.

Open Flightmaps data
The Open Flightmaps (OFM) project (https://www.openflightmaps.org/) is a great project bringing the aeronautical data to the general public for free. Check the license at the web site. They provide the data in several data formats including the OFMX and Openair which can be used in this application.
 
In order to make the airspace setup easier this application implements a semi-automatic update service of the aeronautical data using the data files provided by the OFM in the OFMX format.
 
The Open Flightmaps downloader screen lists areas/regions the OFM initiative maintains and offers a data file for. You can simply choose the region you are flying in and download the data.
 
This is just a shortcut to download, unzip and send the data file to the phone and read it manually. It\'s the Full version feature only. Please purchase the subscription to enable the feature.
 
WARNING: Please note that the data provided by the OFM are not guaranteed and are not intended to be used as primary source of data for the in flight navigation! They might be inaccurate, incomplete and/or irrelevant.
 
Note: Older devices with low memory have problems loading and parsing the very big air space files and may crash with Out of memory error. Then you need a newer device with more memory.

Settings
- Use pressure altitude - Check this box if you want to see pressure altitude on main screen instead of GPS altitude. It\'s either/or. This option has only impact to the main screen altitude view. Don\'t forget to set your local QNH (below transition level) or standard QNH (above transition altitude) in the QNH option in order to see correct local altitude. Just bear in mind how precise your phone pressure sensor is!
 
- QNH - current QNH - local QNH below transition level, standard 1013 above transition altitude. This option is only used if Pressure altitude option is checked.
 
- Vertical profile - an extra settings screen for the vertical profile / situation indicator.
 
- Screen orientation - choose portrait or landscape screen orientation for the whole application. You need to exit the application and start again in order to apply the changed option.
 
- Full brightness - Enable this option to shine the phone at maximum brightness during flight. It\'s recommended for flying.
 
- Dark map theme - choose between a dark and a light main screen map theme. It really depends on your preference. Some areas look better dark, some others look better light… it also depends on the air space setup.
 
- Contrast main scr. UI - shows all the main screen numeric values in high contrast (white).
 
- Background timer - it can happen that you close the application by mistake during the flight or you \'get lost\' on another application and you can\'t get back to the right application. This timer ensures that wherever you are in Android you allways get back to the Aviator main screen. It\'s very useful and recommended to keep set for the best flight experience. However you can switch it off if you set it to 0.
 
- Map location timer - similarly you can scroll in the map somewhere and get lost in space. No worries, the application returns you back after the time expires (after the last map interaction). And again, setting it to 0 switches the timer off.
 
- GPS Altitude correction - the WGS84 world model doesn\'t fit precisely to the real altitude in the whole world. You should adjust your GPS altitude to the real value. Just use some known reference point and let the GPS altimeter show you the best possible altitude.
 
- Top Airspace FL/alt. filter - the highest altitude / flight level you care - from the air space definition file point of view. All air spaces with a low limit above this value are not shown. This is just to reduce amount of information on screen.
 
- Default map zoom - defines the map zoom level used when the view is centered to your current location and when it follows your flight. It uses Google maps zoom level system.
 
- FP turn point radius - the distance to the active flight plan turn point which is considered as reaching the turn point so a next turn point is activated.
 
- XContest settings - extra screen with settings for integration with server xcontest.org.
 
- Show POIs - show / hide POIs (points of interest) - interesting places, must see places. This is an experimental feature not fully implemented yet. The POIs are shown as violet markers on map. A this moment there is just few of them in the whole world. They should be created by the community… so feel free to add new ones. You can do it by a long press on the map - a menu is open, choose \'Register a new POI\' to register a new POI. It will not be shown in the map… this is a server side manual action at the moment.

Location sharing
The location sharing allows you to share your location with other pilots using this application. All you need is to put a nick name and activate it. If you exit the application the location sharing is stopped and you have to manually re-enable it again to share your location. If you enable the Location sharing auto start the sharing will be started automatically every time you launch the application. You can only see your friends if you are also sharing your location.
 
You can leave the group name empty and then you see all pilots in this unnamed default group. Or you can put there a unique name, share this name with your friends and only the same group members will see each other in the air.
 
This feature is only available in the Full version. Please purchase the subscription to enable the feature.

Vertical profile
This is an extra screen for enabling and showing vertical flight profile and its properties. The vertical profile shows the most important information about current vertical situation - below and above you. It consists of:
- Ground elevation
- Low height (above ground level altitude) warnings
- Current (active) air spaces situation
…and of course you, the flying pilot!  
The whole vertical profile indicator is shown on right side of the screen.
The ground elevation is being obtained via a simple remote web service call for the whole world for latitudes between 60 and -60 degrees. Out of this area the ground level altitude is always zero (0). So if you want to use the vertical profile make sure you have active a data plan allowing you continuous online web requests during the flight. The world is divided to small squares of approx. 230x230 metres and a new request is sent anytime you leave actual square. It causes requests being sent one in several seconds.
 
WARNING:
Please note that the ground elevation is calculated as interpolation of the square corners\' elevation which means that the true ground elevation is NOT precise, especially in hilly areas! Understand the ground level more as an additional low importance, non precise information.
The ground elevation (above sea level) is shown as wider brown bottom part of the bar.
 
The low height warnings are represented by 2 defined minimum heights above the ground level - 1) for flying above free terrain (red, by default 150m) and 2) above urban area (yellow, by default 300m). These areas are displayed in the vertical profile just above the ground level elevation. If you don\'t want to use them, just set their value(s) to zero.
 
Additionally it shows any air space around your present altitude so you see if you are below / in / above any air space. Color of the air space indicator corresponds to the air space color shown on map view. If here are more spaces at the same location and their bottom and top altitudes/flight levels, overlap, only one of the colliding spaces are shown (and it\'s undefined which one).
 
Finally the most important is of course your current vertical position. It\'s indicated by a small white point / rectangle / spot.
 
The vertical situation profile indicator shows only relative information, not an absolute altitude. The bars and their colors depend on your current location (air space configuration) and your actual altitude / height / flight level.

XContest settings
This is an extra settings screen for integration with the xcontest.org server. You need to set up all the values in this screen before you can upload your IGC files to the server.
 
The User name and Password are your xcontest.org credentials. You need also fill in your real Pilot name which will be included in the IGC flight file. Then you need to name your Glider type. Finally you need to choose the correct value for FAI class and FAI wing category.
